minutes.headline: Commission plans a March vote on final design guidelines; fee and abutters-list questions left open pending research.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met on Zoom only because of the snow forecast. It approved the prior minutes, discussed recruiting a new member, and reviewed proposed changes to the design guidelines and certificate to alter process, including fees and abutters lists. The chair will research fees, talk to Nathan about 50 Main Street, and bring final guidelines to the next meeting.

votes.motion: Accept the prior meeting minutes as presented; seconded.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair got no answer from the town clerk's office on who sets fees and found no fee listed, so proposed dropping it. Richard said a fee was set to cover the land use secretary's time.
The chair said newspaper notices would now come out of the commission's own budget. Members felt a fee to cover that extraordinary expense could be justified.
Members agreed no fee should be charged for the intermediate form asking whether a certificate to alter is needed.

decisions.decision: Members to review the redlined guidelines and reply by email whether to proceed to a final copy for the next meeting.
No fee for the preliminary form asking whether a certificate to alter is needed.
Chair to research fees with the land use office and town manager, and likely keep an abutters list requirement, possibly with envelopes and stamps.
Aim to vote on new and abbreviated guidelines in March, then bring them to the select board.
Next meeting set for the 12th of March.
Chair to talk to Ann Aubrey about fees and workload and to Nathan about 50 Main Street.

The chair will research fees with the land use office and town manager; an abutters list requirement will likely stay.

why_it_matters: Anyone planning exterior work on a building in the Architectural Preservation District could face changed paperwork, a possible fee for a certificate to alter, and an abutters-list requirement once the new guidelines are adopted.
Hearing notices now draw on the commission's own budget, which is why a fee is being discussed, and nobody has yet established who sets such fees.
